the model says the meaning changed: The requirement and DEC-260 say the third failure in a row goes to the debug workflow, but the worker now opens no debug case when the failing step is "dispatch" (model unreachable), which weakens EX-10 for that case.; filed as a question for the owner, to ask with the question tool: What you asked for: plumb's model work runs as background jobs, is retried when it fails, and never falls back to word rules when no model can be reached. The requirement says a failing job is retried at the next turn end, up to 3 times, and the third failure in a row goes to debugging (EX-10). You confirmed this later: retry first with a larger budget each time, and the third failure in a row becomes a debug case. The requirement and your intent still agree.

What changed: the worker now skips the debug case when the failure was "no model could be reached". The code comment explains why: an outage is a problem with the setup, not a plumb bug, and a bigger budget can't fix it. So if the model is unreachable at three turn ends in a row, nothing goes to debugging, and EX-10's "one case went to debugging" no longer happens for that kind of failure.

What's unclear: the change looks deliberate and the reason makes sense. But nothing in the latest message I found asked for it (that message was a handover note from another session), and your earlier answer doesn't make an exception for outages. I can't tell whether you wanted this. It also doesn't say what the turn-end plumb line should show in this case, or whether the job keeps being retried after the third failure.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Undo the change: three failures in a row always go to debugging, outages included") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Keep the change: say in the requirement that an unreachable model at the third failure doesn't go to debugging, and the plumb line says plumb couldn't reach a model") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Keep the exception, but still stop retrying after the third failure and tell you plainly that the model is unreachable") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (plumb stale card SR-273#16 --consequences "..." --why "...")

the model says the meaning changed: The requirement says the third failure in a row of a judge job writes one debug case (EX-5) and that every plumb failure opens a case, but the worker now writes no case when the failing step is "dispatch", so that failure is silently dropped.; filed as a question for the owner, to ask with the question tool: What you asked for: when plumb itself fails, including a judge job failing for the third time in a row, plumb opens a debug case. The requirement says the same thing: the third failure in a row of a judge job writes one case (example EX-5), and every plumb failure opens a case.

What changed: the code no longer opens a case when the failure happened at the "dispatch" step. That is the step where plumb looks for a model to send the job to. The comment in the code says that having no model to ask is a problem with the environment, not with plumb, and a bigger budget can't fix it. So when a judge job fails three times in a row because no model is available, no case is opened, and the failure isn't reported anywhere.

What's unclear: your intent is about plumb's own failures, so leaving out environment problems could be what you want. But neither the requirement nor the intent makes that exception, and the latest prompt (a handover message from another session) didn't ask for this change. Only you can say whether failures to reach a model should open a debug case, be reported some other way, or be ignored.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Keep the change: reword the requirement so that a failure because no model is available doesn't open a debug case") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Keep leaving it out of the debug cases, but report that failure some other way (for example, mention once that no model is available)") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Undo the change: every third failure in a row opens a debug case, including when no model is available") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (plumb stale card SR-325#8 --consequences "..." --why "...")
